speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) whether the Ministry has completed its review of the Australian government's move to ban social media access for individuals under the age of 16 through legislation; and (b) if so, whether the Ministry will consider introducing similar legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The age assurance measures will come on top of the existing protective measures for children under the current Code of Practice for Online Safety – Social Media Services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Consultations with designated social media services are ongoing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: We acknowledge parental concerns about the impact of social media on their children as well as the potential implementation challenges of age assurance requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: A child can still circumvent these measures, such as through using an adult's account to access age-inappropriate content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: This is why MDDI will continue to work with partners from the people, private and public sectors, to co-create resources and programmes that are convenient and accessible for parents to help guide their children to foster healthy digital habits from young.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And I think the age assurance practices are probably a good first step.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I would just like to clarify whether the social media platforms are then required to take steps to prevent these young users from using those platforms.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Because I think there are two issues: one is harmful content, and the second is addiction to the platforms itself even if the content may not be ostensibly harmful.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, that is why a clean block and putting the obligation on the social media platform to verify age before the users are allowed to use it, sounds like a tidy solution – and that is what they have done in Australia.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It is not perfect, but it sets a clear line.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: How we have been looking at this issue is that, yes, indeed, it is not just a function of accessing it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There are three main things that we look at.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If you are spending too much time and you are not controlling that, that is a big issue.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And which is why, we then need to have certain measures to make sure that children are not exposed to this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we are categorising and looking at the multi-dimensional effect of the social media platforms.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: While the legislative changes that the Member is hearing which are happening in other countries sound very attractive and seem like an obvious solution, what I think we want to ensure is a meaningful implementation that will actually make a difference in the experience of the children and the parents.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would want to highlight a couple of points.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There was an observation that there was a migration of children or the users to platforms that are not within the regulatory ambit.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we have to make sure that if we do this, it is something that will be quite meaningful.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we need to make sure that the enforcement measures are clear cut because children can use their parents' identification, so, the structure needs to be in place there.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There was also a rise in virtual private networks, which then, undermines all these.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we want to make sure that we can address some of those concerns meaningfully.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, I would highlight that we are not starting from a blank slate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is not like we do not have measures in place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have not been prescriptive with how age assurance measures are put in, because even for age assurance, you have age verification and age estimation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These are some of the things that we know we want to allow platforms to put in.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We say, "You must put in place these things to ensure that children are not exposed to these things." How they actually do that is something that they have to look at in their circumstances.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There are already some structures in place to provide safeguards and ensure that it is a healthy ecosystem for children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And the third thing is that we are doing more.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are actually looking at how we can continue to improve regulatory infrastructure to support this and we take a multi-prong approach.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, it is not just about having the legislation; it is also about building capability within the community, and which is why I mentioned about helping to build healthy digital habits and providing support for parents through resources and programmes on the ground.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is something that we will be ramping up in time.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I hope that this is something that we can work together on because there are multiple stakeholders: parents have to play a part, the regulators, the social media platforms.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, we are in close contact with them to ensure that they are doing their best.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are trying to figure out what is the best solution in these circumstances.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I hope that gives an appreciation that we are really appreciating and understanding the concerns and we are trying to figure out a robust approach that fits and would be meaningful for parents and children in Singapore.
